<reason>Side B established that early starts constrain adolescent sleep, but Side A more convincingly showed that permitting sleep is not enough to justify a universal mandate. A sustained the evening-shift, long-commute, elementary-transfer, and unfunded-cost objections, while B answered funding and rural cases mainly with potential gains and future mitigation. A's local-choice alternative preserved later starts without accepting certain costs for uncertain benefits.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>Side A's Rebuttal 2 was decisive: it directly accepted that early starts constrain sleep, then turned B's guarantee-versus-permission framing against the mandate by arguing that a mere possibility cannot override immediate family, transport, and younger-child costs in every district.</best_rebuttal>
